'''Luis Ernesto Miramontes Cárdenas''' (March 16, 1925 – September 13, 2004) was a Mexican chemist known as co-inventor and the first to synthesize an oral contraceptive, [[progestin]] [[norethisterone]].

==Career summary==

Miramontes was born in [[Tepic]], [[Nayarit]]. He obtained his first Degree in chemical engineering at the [[Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México]] (UNAM). He was a founding researcher of the Institute of Chemistry of UNAM, specializing mainly in the area of [[Organic Chemistry]]. He was a professor of the Faculty of Chemistry of UNAM, Director and professor of the School of Chemistry at the [[Universidad Iberoamericana]], and deputy director of research at the [[Mexican Institute of Petroleum]] (IMP). Miramontes was a member the [[American Chemical Society]] (Emeritus), the Mexican Institute of Chemical Engineers, the National Institute of Chemical and Chemical Engineers, the Chemical Society of Mexico, the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]] and the [[New York Academy of Sciences]]. He died in [[Mexico City]] in 2004.

The scientific contributions of Luis Miramontes are extensive, including numerous publications and nearly 40 national and international patents in different areas such as [[organic chemistry]], [[pharmaceutical chemistry]], [[petrochemistry]] and [[atmospheric chemistry]] and polluting agents.

==First synthesis of an oral contraceptive==
[[File:Miramontes_rosenkranz_2001.jpg|left|200px|thumb|[[George Rosenkranz]] (right) and Luis E. Miramontes (left), 2001 at the [[UNAM]]]]
On October 15, 1951, under the supervision of [[Carl Djerassi]] and the direction of [[George Rosenkranz]] at [[Syntex]] laboratory in Mexico City, Miramontes completed the first ever synthesis of an oral contraceptive: progestin norethisterone.

While Djerassi is sometimes regarded as 'Father of the Pill'".,<ref name=autogenerated1>Penny Le Couteur & Jay Burreson. ''Napoleon's Buttons''. Tarcher; Reprint edition (May 24, 2004)</ref> it was Miramontes, working under Djerassi's supervision, that achieved the first synthesis. In the words of Djerassi, "On 15 October 1951, Luis Miramontes, a young Mexican chemist doing his undergraduate bachelor's thesis work at Syntex completed the synthesis of the 19-nor-17α-ethynyltestosterone or, for short 'norethisterone'—which turned out to be the first oral contraceptive to be synthesized.".<ref>Carl Djerassi. ''This Man's Pill: Reflections on the 50th Birthday of the Pill''. Oxford University Press 2001.</ref> Nobel Laureate [[Max Perutz]] added "the chemistry student Luis Miramontes, working under the direction of Djerassi and the director of the laboratory Jorge Rosenkranz synthesized the compound".<ref>Max F. Perutz. I Wish I’d Made You Angry Earlier: Essays on Science, Scientists, and Humanity. Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory Press 1998.</ref>  The last step of the synthesis method was registered on page 114 of the Miramontes's personal laboratory notebook (signed).

All three Miramontes, Djerassi, and Rosenkranz are listed on the patent as co-inventors.

==Recognition==
{{more citations needed section|date=October 2017}}<!--many of these entries are not cited-->
[[File:miramontes patent.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Patent of the first oral contraceptive, elected to the USA Inventors Hall of Fame.]]
*In 1964, the contraceptive pill was chosen by the [[United States Patent and Trademark Office|US Department of Patents]] as one of the 40 registered more important [[inventions]] between 1794 and 1964. The name of Luis Miramontes appeared next to [[Louis Pasteur|Pasteur]], [[Thomas Edison|Edison]], [[Alexander Graham Bell|Bell]], the  [[Wright brothers]] and others of equal stature. It was included in the "USA Inventors Hall of Fame".<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.uspto.gov/learning-and-resources/inventors-entrepreneurs/hispanic-heritage-and-inventions | title=Hispanic Heritage and Inventions | publisher=United States Patent and Trademark Office }}</ref>
*In 1985 he received the "[[Estado de Mexico]]" Medal, in the area of sciences and arts;<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?time_continue=1&v=_QSNijMrpUE&feature=emb_logo | title=Award ceremony of the Presea Edo Mex to Luis E. Miramontes | date=5 January 2010 | publisher=youtube }}</ref> as well as a public recognition from the government of the state of Nayarit, and an academic recognition from the Technological Institute of [[Tepic]].
*He received the Mexican National Prize on Chemistry "[[Andrés Manuel del Rio]]" in 1986.
*In 1989 he became a "[[Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs|pugwashite]]", that is, member of the [[Pugwash Conferences on Science and World Affairs]], organization promoting peace and world development, after attending the  39th Pugwash Conference: Building Global Security through Cooperation held at Cambridge, USA.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/bfm%3A978-3-642-75843-0%2F1.pdf | title= 39th Pugwash Conference: Building Global Security through Cooperation | publisher=Springer }}</ref> The Pugwash Conferences were awarded the Peace [[Nobel Prize]]  in 1995.
*In 1992 the General Hospital of Zone no. 1, of the Mexican Institute of Social Security, in [[Tepic]], [[Nayarit]], was named "Luis Ernesto Miramontes Cardenas Hospital".<ref>{{cite web | url=http://scifunam.fisica.unam.mx/mir/LEMC/reconocimientos/1992-IMSS-Oficio_hospital_Tepic006.jpg | title=Hospital IMSS Luis Ernesto Miramontes Cárdenas | publisher=UNAM | access-date=2019-11-28 | archive-date=2022-11-09 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221109181415/http://scifunam.fisica.unam.mx/mir/LEMC/reconocimientos/1992-IMSS-Oficio_hospital_Tepic006.jpg | url-status=dead }}</ref>
*In 1994 the Mexican Ministry of Health recognized his scientific contributions, when installing the National Program on Family Planning in [[Mexico]].
*He received in 1998, on behalf of the government of the state of [[Nayarit]], the "Amado Nervo" Medal.
[[File:mario molina.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Luis E. Miramontes (right) with Nobel Laureate [[Mario Molina]], ca. 1995]]

*In 2000, the [[combined oral contraceptive pill|contraceptive pill]] was denominated three times as one of the most important inventions of the last 2000 years, by a group of outstanding persons, that included several [[Nobel Prize|Nobel laurates]].<ref>John Brockman, editor. ''The Greatest Inventions of the Past 2000 Years''. Phoenix. 2000</ref>
*In 2001, at the 50th Anniversary of the synthesis of [[norethisterone]], the [[UNAM]] and the Mexican Ministry of Health, organized individual tributes to Miramontes and Rosencraz.
*In 2003, [[norethisterone]] was considered one of the most important 17 molecules that have influenced the history of humankind.<ref name=autogenerated1 />
*In 2004, the invention of Luis E. Miramontes was chosen as the twentieth most important one of all the times. The election was organized by [[SCENTA]], an initiative of The [[Engineering and Technology Board of the United Kingdom]].
*In 2005, the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]], named the invention of Miramontes as the Mexican most important contribution to world science ever.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.gaceta.unam.mx/tag/luis-ernesto-miramontes-cardenas/ | title=La síntesis de un molécula revolucionaria | date=22 March 2019 | publisher=UNAM }}</ref>
*In 2009, the [[BBC]] of London nominated him as one of the five most important Latin American researchers of all the times<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/mundo/ciencia_tecnologia/2009/11/091102_especial_aportes_al_introduccion_mr |title=BBC Mundo – Ciencia y Tecnología – Latinoamericanos que cambiaron el mundo |publisher=Bbc.co.uk |date=1970-01-01 |access-date=2013-10-14}}</ref>
*In 2009, The School of Chemistry of [[UNAM]] recognized him as one of the most successful and important scientists to have received a degree from it<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.quimica.unam.mx/IMG/pdf/gaceta_54_agosto_2009.pdf |language=es |title=Aporte historico y revolucionario de un egresado de la DQ |publisher=Quimica.unam.mx |access-date=2013-10-14 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120301110558/http://www.quimica.unam.mx/IMG/pdf/gaceta_54_agosto_2009.pdf |archive-date=2012-03-01 }}</ref>
*In 2009, The School of Chemistry of [[UNAM]] honored him by naming the 2009 year prize QUIMIUNAM after him.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cienciasquimicas.posgrado.unam.mx/quimiunam/premio.php |title=Quimiunam |publisher=Cienciasquimicas.posgrado.unam.mx |access-date=2013-10-14 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022005824/http://cienciasquimicas.posgrado.unam.mx/quimiunam/premio.php |archive-date=2013-10-22 }}</ref>
*In 2010, TCE Today, published by the [[IChemE]] regarded him "one of the chemical engineers who changed the world" <ref>[http://www.tcetoday.com/chemical%20engineers%20who%20changed%20the%20world.aspx] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110320142112/http://www.tcetoday.com/chemical%20engineers%20who%20changed%20the%20world.aspx|date=March 20, 2011}}</ref>
*In 2010, The Innovators of America initiative nominated him a top Icon & Legend of America<ref>{{cite web |url=http://innovadoresdeamerica.org/app/en/participant_bio.aspx?id=8 |title=Innovadores de America |website=innovadoresdeamerica.org |access-date=17 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726180757/http://innovadoresdeamerica.org/app/en/participant_bio.aspx?id=8 |archive-date=26 July 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
*In 2011 was named one of the world’s most influential chemical engineers of all time by the [[IChemE]] (Institution of Chemical Engineers).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.icheme.org/media_centre/news/2011/haber%20and%20bosch%20named%20top%20chemical%20engineers.aspx |title=Haber and Bosch named top chemical engineers |publisher=Icheme.org |date=2011-02-21 |access-date=2013-10-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005012711/http://www.icheme.org/media_centre/news/2011/haber%20and%20bosch%20named%20top%20chemical%20engineers.aspx |archive-date=2013-10-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* In 2011, The Mexican Institute of Chemical Engineers [[IMIQ]] named after him the Prize "Ing. Luis Ernesto Miramontes Cárdenas" aimed to recognize outstanding Mexicans in Chemical Engineering R&D.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://imiq.com.mx/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=209&Itemid=303 |title=Ing. Luis E. Miramontes |publisher=Imiq.com.mx |access-date=2013-10-14}}</ref>

Luis E. Miramontes, [[Andrés Manuel del Río]] (discoverer of [[vanadium]]) and [[Mario Molina]], Chemistry [[Nobel Prize]] in 1995, are the three most important Mexican chemists of all time.
